correctness.rationale: A two-agent cross-edge swap is strictly profitable in one orientation iff (k-h-1)(b-n-1)<0 and (k-h-1)(b-n+1)>0. Integrality forces b=n and k-h>1; reversing sides gives h-k>1. Every same-part swap leaves the neighbor multiset unchanged, and same-color swaps are inert. Counting the stable k yields the three exact binomial formulas; Stirling gives parity-dependent asymptotics. The stand-alone direct best-response checker exhausts all colorings on K_{n,n} for n=2..6, with both moving agents compared at their destinations; the infinite proof does not rely on finite enumeration.

value.rationale: This is a complete equilibrium classification on an infinite, natural bipartite network family for a distinct open-neighborhood preference formulation. It reveals that a one-agent population perturbation destroys an otherwise vanishing-stable-fraction equilibrium restriction: all nonbalanced compositions are universally stable while exactly balanced compositions retain only order n^(-1/2) of colorings. This explicit discontinuity is a meaningful structural boundary rather than a routine parameter example.
